## Common-tier retail bot "learning" mechanisms — gap analysis vs this repo

**1. Indicator/strategy parameter grid search (Freqtrade Hyperopt, Optuna backend)**
Learns: numeric thresholds (RSI bounds, EMA lengths, stop%, ROI table) by minimizing a backtest loss over historical OHLCV. Evidence standard: none by default — pure in-sample loss minimization; walk-forward split is opt-in and rarely enforced [K WebSearch: freqtrade.io/en/stable/hyperopt/, botacademy.ddns.net 2025-04-02]. Failure literature: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu, "The Probability of Backtest Overfitting" (J. Computational Finance, 2016) — formalizes PBO/CSCV for exactly this parameter-sweep pattern; Harvey & Liu, "Backtesting" (J. Portfolio Management, 2015) — p-hacking via repeated trials without multiple-testing correction; Bailey & López de Prado, "The Deflated Sharpe Ratio" (J. Portfolio Management, 2014).
Repo: this pattern is absent by design. `Grep` for `hyperopt|optuna|grid_search` across the tree returns zero files. No decision-path threshold is fit by backtest loss minimization; thresholds live in `config.json` with `core/config_guard.py` FATAL checks per CLAUDE.md ("no fitted-looking literals"). The repo's PBO instrument (`scripts/overfit_check.py` OF-3, `c:\Users\haird\Documents\liquiditybot\liquiditybot_ab\scripts\overfit_check.py:22-24`, docstring cites CSCV) is the *audit* Bailey et al. prescribe for this failure mode, run against the deployed simplicity-ladder selection rule, never argmax — directly the discipline the Hyperopt tier skips.

**2. FreqAI (Freqtrade's supervised ML layer: LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost regressors+classifiers on TA features)**
Learns: price-direction/return labels from engineered TA features, retrained on a rolling window ("adaptive modelling"). Evidence standard: FreqAI docs flag it "experimental," recommend backtesting with `--timerange` splits but ship no purge/embargo, no shuffle-null, no PBO on model selection; overfitting/local-minima risk explicitly acknowledged by the maintainers [K WebSearch: freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai/]. Failure literature: López de Prado, *Advances in Financial Machine Learning* (Wiley, 2018) ch. 7 (purged/embargoed CV) and ch. 8 (feature importance via MDA) — the exact gaps FreqAI's rolling-retrain leaves open; Cerqueira, Torgo & Mozetič, "Evaluating Time Series Forecasting Models" (Machine Learning, 2020) on CV leakage in serially correlated data.
Repo: same family of model (gbt/mlp/logistic in `ml/models.py`, `c:\Users\haird\Documents\liquiditybot\liquiditybot_ab\ml\models.py`), but retrain evidence is gated, not assumed: `ml/walkforward.py` implements purged walk-forward (consumed by OF-1/OF-2/OF-6 per `scripts/overfit_check.py:7-21,715`), `ml/overfit.py:train_test_gap` is OF-1, and OF-2 (`overfit_check.py:18-21`) is the shuffled-label null FreqAI lacks entirely. Current honest state per ground truths: all three model families lose OOF Brier to the base-rate null (0.28-0.435 vs 0.165) — this repo *reports* that as unproven edge rather than deploying on backtest fit, which is the FreqAI-tier gap. Model-side investment is frozen (era-4 moratorium, CLAUDE.md) precisely because the corpus (11,312 rows, mean_uniqueness 0.152, ~600-1000 post-dedup) hasn't earned added capacity — evidence-gated capacity is the correct answer to FreqAI's "just retrain more" default.

**3. Hummingbot market-making / pure market-making strategy with adaptive spread controllers**
Learns: nothing statistical by default — spreads/order sizes are rule-based (inventory skew, volatility multiplier via NATR); "AI livestream"/Gateway ML add-ons exist but the core loop is a fixed-parameter controller, occasionally hand-tuned against a paper-trade sample. Evidence standard: paper-trade duration is operator-chosen, no formal OOS boundary; success is read off cumulative PnL on one continuous run — classic non-independent-trials illusion (Harvey & Liu 2015; White, "A Reality Check for Data Snooping," Econometrica 2000). Failure literature: White (2000) Reality Check, Romano & Wolf, "Stepwise Multiple Testing" (Econometrica 2005) — both target exactly the single-run-looks-good fallacy this tier relies on.
Repo: comparable component is `execution/hedging.py` inventory hedger + `risk/` protocol stack — rule-based, not backtest-fit, and CLAUDE.md forbids exactly the failure mode (no "temporarily" bypassing dry_run to get a live read). **4. DCA/grid bots ("smart" variants with volatility-scaled grid spacing)**
Learns: grid width from realized/ATR volatility, sometimes a "backtested" grid density chosen by max-drawdown-vs-return scan over one historical window. Evidence standard: essentially none — single-window optimization, frequently marketed on win-rate% with no cost model (maker/taker fees, funding) and no distinction between mean-reverting and trending regimes it will blow up in. Failure literature: same Bailey/Harvey/López de Prado cluster above; additionally Lopez de Prado's DSR directly answers the "73% win rate" red flag pattern (many small wins, one fat tail loss — Sharpe/DSR punishes this, raw win-rate doesn't).
Repo: `risk/` CVaR/gap/budget/heat stack (RiskProtocolStack per CLAUDE.md architecture section) and `ProfitTierEngine` + give-back ratchet are the analog of grid/DCA exit logic, but sized through drawdown-aware risk math, not a single-window drawdown scan. `scripts/overfit_check.py` OF-4 (plateau, `overfit_check.py:25-29`) is the direct antidote to the grid-bot failure mode: a real edge sits on a parameter plateau, a curve-fit grid spacing sits on a spike — though ground truths flag OF-4 is currently inert here (replay opens zero positions in the current corpus), so this repo cannot yet claim OF-4 clears for its own strategy either.

**5. "Simple supervised classifier on TA features" (logistic/RF on RSI/MACD/BB, no purging)**
Learns: P(price up) from a feature vector, trained with vanilla k-fold CV — the single most common retail ML mistake because k-fold shuffles serially correlated, overlapping-label financial data, leaking future information across folds. Evidence standard: train/test accuracy reported, rarely OOF AUC, almost never purge/embargo. Failure literature: López de Prado (2018) ch. 7 is the canonical fix (purged k-fold + embargo); this is the single most-cited gap in the retail-ML-bot literature.
Repo: this exact leakage class is what OF-2's shuffled-label null exists to catch (`overfit_check.py:18-21`, "Catches purge bugs, feature peeking, index misalignment") and `ml/walkforward.py` implements the purge itself — the repo has already built the standard fix; the open question is corpus size, not methodology (base-rate-null loss is a signal-absence finding, not a leakage finding — 29/64 near-zero-importance features are live-verified, per ground truths, ruling out a feed bug as the cause).

### Defining epistemic weakness of the common tier
Every mechanism above shares one structural flaw: **the evaluation sample is not held independent of the selection decision.** Whether the selection is a hyperopt loss, a FreqAI retrain window, a hand-tuned grid spacing, or an eyeballed paper-trade run, the same historical (or short live) window both proposes and grades the parameter/model — the precise degenerate case PBO (Bailey et al. 2016) and the Reality Check (White 2000) were built to detect. Headline win-rates/Sharpes from this tier carry no correction for the number of implicit trials (strategies, parameter combos, retrain windows) tried before the one reported — so a 73% backtest win rate is evidence of a search process, not an edge, until it clears purged OOS, a shuffle null, PBO on the *deployed* selection rule, and a deflated Sharpe — exactly the four gates `scripts/overfit_check.py` runs (OF-1/2/3/5) and this repo has not yet let its own strategy claim victory on (base-rate-null loss across all three model families, per ground truths).

## 4. Bayesian sizing under parameter uncertainty
- Lit: Kelly (1956) full-Kelly baseline; fractional-Kelly under estimation error (MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2011 survey) — shows naive-Kelly is fragile to win-rate estimation error, motivates shrinkage/fractional or full posterior-predictive sizing (Bayesian Kelly, e.g. Baker & McHale 2012).
- Repo: fractional Kelly implemented, uncertainty handled by a fixed shrinkage constant, not a posterior: `risk/position_sizer.py:103-104` (`kelly_fraction=0.25`, `kelly_cap=0.12` from config), sizing computed at lines 410-486 (`f = max(f_star,0.0) * self.kelly_fraction; f = min(f, self.kelly_cap)`). verdicts.reason: Arithmetic re-derived and correct: 1000/2.8-3.3 = 303-357d; 64x10=640 floor / 2.8-3.3 = 194-229d; live-labeled 333 [K]; ~3 honest rows/day [K]. Counterfactual training share re-derived: (600-333)/600=44.5%, (1000-333)/1000=66.7% — matches claimed 45-67% [I, correct given loader keeps 600-1000 and ALL 333 live rows survive dedup; if dedup drops live rows the share is HIGHER, strengthening the claim]. 'Program lifetime' is vague, but era-4 horizons are ~25-28 days (readout ~9-10d + n=100 extension ~15-18d per decision table 3A), vs 194+ days to even the 10x floor on live-only — two orders apart, the gap survives any reasonable definition. Honest caveat carried: the design never intended live-only convergence (merged corpus is the diet by design), so P2's bite is conditional on the candidate-to-live transfer question — which P2 itself names as its decider, and which the calibration read (predicted 0.29 -> realized 0.07 on live-ish buckets [K, elimination doc :44-45]) currently supports in P2's direction. Cross-source flag: elimination doc :67 says 44/50 accrued vs truths block 21/50 — does not affect the rate arithmetic, both sources carry ~3/day.

And CLAUDE.md's moratorium section literally frames it as 'The strategy verdict accrues on the era-4 honest-fill cohort' [K] — so the juxtaposition (record calls it the strategy verdict; record simultaneously proves the admission stream is probe-only and production admits nothing) is real, not constructed. verdicts.claim: P4 — $800 makes every learned lesson non-portable.
verdicts.reason: The universal quantifier fails against the truths block's own numbers. The dominant negative finding — gross expectancy -0.5..-0.73%/path PRE-COST and hit rate 14-20pp below label-geometry breakeven [K] — is computed before fees, min-ticket quantization, or fill costs enter. It is therefore size-invariant: the no-edge lesson ports to $50k unchanged, and zero fee tier rescues a pre-cost-negative geometry. Second, the fill-scarcity causality is backwards: a $15 ticket needs LESS book flow to fill than a large order at the same price level; small size improves fill probability, it does not worsen it. The 28 timeout-cancels vs 3 fills [K] indicts limit PLACEMENT (price never reached), which is capital-independent — not capital. What survives are sub-facts that do not carry the claim: fee-tier pinning is real ($1.35-3.6k/30d re-derived correctly, bottom tier permanent [K]), and min ticket = 1.875% of capital checks. So SOME execution-cost lessons are genuinely non-portable — but 'every learned lesson' is refuted, and the claim's own refuter condition ('dominant loss terms are size-invariant') is already satisfied by [K] pre-cost negativity, no afternoon of decomposition needed. Self-check on my refutation: could adverse selection make small fills WORSE per-fill? No — adverse selection conditions on being filled, not on size; if anything larger orders suffer more of it.

verdicts.reason: (Claim truncated mid-sentence in my input; ruled on the stated load-bearing content.) All arithmetic re-derived: 10979/11312 = 97.06% candidate [K]; counterfactual training share 44.5-66.7% matches claimed 45-67% [I, correct, and conservative — dedup dropping live rows would raise it]; live fill rate 3/(3+28) = 9.7% per 48h read [K]. The gate_efficacy doc :7-9 confirms CandidateLabeler labels every gate-confirmed signal, admitted or vetoed, as outcome-labeled counterfactual [K] — 'as if executable' is a fair paraphrase. The bias direction (touch=fill, zero queue, zero adverse selection -> counterfactual labels optimistic vs realized fills) is [I] on labeler mechanics, but it is the textbook direction AND the record independently corroborates it: p(win) biased HIGH across nearly every bucket, predicted 0.29 -> realized 0.07 n=211 [K, elimination doc :44-45] — exactly the signature of a model fed optimistic counterfactual labels then graded on real outcomes. Nothing in the truths block or the primaries contradicts it; the calib-gap improvement (0.079->0.031) does not refute it because that gap is measured within the retrain loop's own (majority-counterfactual) diet. The one unverifiable piece is whatever followed the truncation; the visible claim survives.
